sections.html: The genus Auchenipterus is closely related to, and similar to, Epapterus and Pseudepapterus. Family: Auchenipteridae. Size: 25 cm. Temperature: 23-26°C. pH: 6.5-7.2.
This species will not be seen too often in the hobby.
South America: Upper and middle Amazon and Orinoco River basins and coastal rivers of Guyana. Type locality: Ambyiacu River, Ecuador.

Can be fed most aquarium fare such as good quality flake, white worm, tablet and pellet foods and frozen foods such as bloodworm. Better to feed at lights out until they get accustomed to the daytime feeding regime, when they may very well join in.
A good catfish for a large aquarium with normal sized tankmates, but not to be trusted with small tetras, for instance, which will be picked off at night on its twilight patrols.

A. ambyiacus is distinguished from all congeners by the following combination of characters: anal fin origin located anterior of the middle of the body; caudal fin with tip of lobes dark; pelvic fin darkly pigmented on its leading edge and, often, on the distal margin; typically 49-51 vertebrae and 36-39 gill rakers on the outer edge of the first arch. It is most similar in appearance to A. osteomystax, from which it is most easily distinguished by the higher gill raker counts in the latter species (typically 43-46).

Etymology: The specific name ambyiacus: -acus (L.), belonging to: Ambyiacu (also spelled Ampiyacu) River, Ecuador, type locality.

IUCN Red List: Despite there being little information available on this species, it is assessed as Least Concern due to its wide range and no direct threats (IUCN 2023).
